name: Osteomyelitis of Long Bone
definition: Infection of bone caused by hematogenous spread, contiguous infection, trauma or surgery, potentially leading to necrosis and chronic sinus formation.

typical: Persistent wound or sinus in chronic disease

investigations.principle: Diagnosis requires clinical, laboratory, microbiological and imaging correlation.
investigations.MRI: MRI is the most sensitive imaging test for many forms of osteomyelitis.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs may be initially normal but later show destruction/periosteal change.

amber: Do not delay antibiotics in septic/unstable patients; chronic infection often needs multidisciplinary orthopedic/infectious-disease care.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Asthi-gata infection should not be managed by Ayurvedic correlation alone; modern infection control is mandatory.

patientEducation.summary: Infection of bone caused by hematogenous spread, contiguous infection, trauma or surgery, potentially leading to necrosis and chronic sinus formation.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for severe/progressive neurological deficit, vascular compromise, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, sphincter change or other listed red flags.
